chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, linking it up through his chain to Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), saying:

People are of four types: Some have good character but no wealth; some have wealth but no good character; some have neither good character nor wealth, and they are the worst of people; and some have both good character and wealth, and they are the best of people.

key_terms.خُلُق: Good character, manners, or moral disposition
key_terms.يَرْفَعُهُ: Linking it up (referring to the chain of narration connecting to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of people according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes humanity into four archetypes based on the interplay between innate moral character (khuluq) and acquired merit or wealth (khallaq), a distinction often interpreted in Shia scholarship as balancing spiritual virtue with worldly status. The 'best of people' are those who possess both inner nobility and external standing, while those lacking both are deemed the worst, highlighting the ideal integration of ethics and influence. This classification serves as a practical guide for evaluating societal roles and personal development within the community.
